question.text: What happens to the purchasing power of Rs.100 after 5 years if inflation is consistently at 5% per annum?

answer.text: It remains Rs.100 in real terms
It is equivalent to approximately Rs.78 in today's terms
It is equivalent to approximately Rs.95 in today's terms
It increases to Rs.128 in real terms

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook, the purchasing-power/inflation concept is introduced on page 18 and revisited on page 73, with page 19 providing a 5% over 5-year illustration. Discounting Rs.100 by 5% per year compounded over 5 years gives Rs.100/(1.05)^5 = Rs.100/1.2763, or about Rs.78.35 in today's terms. The Trap: Option C (Rs.95) understates the erosion by ignoring compounding altogether, while option A assumes no inflation impact and option D reverses the direction of the adjustment. Note: Always use the compound-discount formula (divide by (1+i)^n) rather than a simple 5% x 5 = 25% deduction; the compounding effect is what makes inflation so corrosive over long retirement horizons.
